column4: Visit note | 2025-03-04 03:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rezaul Haque, 74, male. Mr. Haque reports feeling nauseous with a spinning sensation and dizziness whenever he looks up. He mentions that the trouble began after a viral cold in Khilgaon. He works as a madrasa teacher and struggles with his daily lessons when the room seems to tilt. He has no history of chronic illnesses, and denies headaches, ear pain, or weakness in his limbs. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 127/83 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 84 kg. Neurological exam shows normal cranial nerves and no focal deficits. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
